claims.proof_role: tight-frame recovery of the classical Bussemaker--Mathon--Seidel order-six switching normal form, matching expansion of the Pfaffian, Hodge middle-exterior comparison, and the golden eigenspace block decomposition.  The scalar-square implication and sign-matrix converse are formalized in the four-shadow gate; the manuscript proves the real positivity statement by translation invariance of the triangle cubic: its tx_i x_j coefficients force A^2 diagonal, and commutation makes that diagonal scalar; equal absolute values then recover the pentagon gauge.  The coherence of the outer six-family and the cross-golden comparison are formalized: each of the six relabelled conference matrices is symmetric with vanishing diagonal, unit off-diagonal squares and square 5*I, the six sign words are distinct and each obeys the four-point identity, and over a commutative ring with two invertible and an invertible square root s of five the commutator of the diagonal matrix with the conference matrix is 2s times the antisymmetric part of the cross-golden block, whence Z^2 = 500 det(B - B^T) and, exactly, Z = 10 s Pf(B - B^T), an identity unchanged by using the other square root of five.  The determinant of the induced map between the two spectral spaces is a determinant-line element; after compatible orientations, the odd-rank contraction is minus its ordinary quadratic field norm.  The rigidity statement is proved in the manuscript by Euler homogeneity, the multilinear difference rule for the twenty equations, equivariance under the order-sixty stabilizer, a fixed-vector reduction to a five-dimensional space, the displayed reduced table with its minus-five minor, and the constant-rank theorem; its table is certified against the manuscript's own representative and sign convention by a dated evidence bundle retained in the source archive, and the rank statement itself is not formalized.  The sign-locus characterization is proved in the manuscript from two elementary facts about three-by-three sign matrices and the identity relating a complementary block's row inner products to the square, with an exhaustive order-six census as the independent check.
claims.statement: For a fully marked golden presentation, the triangle cubic, the diagonal of the middle exterior return, the commutator Pfaffian, and the determinant of the cross-golden block define the same oriented cubic, with Pf[D_x,C_T]=4Z_T, det[D_x,C_T]=16Z_T^2=-8000 N(det(B_T)), and Z_T=plus-or-minus 10 sqrt(5) det(B_T). Conversely, for a real symmetric even-order zero-diagonal matrix with nonzero off-diagonal entries, nonzero proportionality of its commutator Pfaffian and triangle cubic forces order six and A^2=lambda I; on the equal-absolute-value locus this is exactly the pentagon conference class, with the two proportionality signs recording relative orientation. The equality is locally rigid at either oriented golden representative, its Jacobian having rank fourteen with kernel the scaling line; and on the sign locus the cubic identity may be replaced by the nondegeneracy of all twenty complementary three-by-three minors, which forces the same class and makes the proportionality constant plus or minus four the only value available.

The manuscript's printed proof instead closes the rigidity direction by the characteristic-zero inclusion-rank descent, a switching normalization, and the Ramsey equality R(3,3)=6, whose two bounds are kernel-checked though no Lean declaration states the equality itself; the Lean therefore certifies the theorem's conclusion by a different route than the one printed, and the manuscript integration that would align them has not been made.
